description: Table 5, rendered as an image, is a plain data table titled "Example of hardening effects of cellular transformation and spinodal decomposition". It has a left column headed "Composition (wt%)" and a right header "Hardness [HV]" split into two sub-columns, "Hot-rolled" and "800 °C — Tempere" (the final characters are cut off at the right image edge). Four Fe–Mn–Al–C lightweight-steel compositions are tabulated exactly as printed: 9Al-10Mn-1C, 12Al-10Mn-1C, 12Al-20Mn-1C and 12Al-30Mn1C. Hardness values in HV are: 9Al-10Mn-1C 273 → 356; 12Al-10Mn-1C 401 → 399; 12Al-20Mn-1C 357 → 404; 12Al-30Mn1C 324 → 352 (hot-rolled versus 800 °C tempered). Three of four alloys gain hardness on tempering, the largest gain being 12Al-20Mn-1C (357 to 404 HV), whereas 12Al-10Mn-1C is essentially unchanged (401 vs 399 HV) and already the hardest in the hot-rolled state; the hardest tempered state is 404 HV. The table shows that the phases formed by cellular transformation and spinodal decomposition at 800 °C raise hardness, but not for every composition.

observations.observation: The table's composition column lists four alloys exactly as printed: 9Al-10Mn-1C, 12Al-10Mn-1C, 12Al-20Mn-1C and 12Al-30Mn1C (no hyphen in the last one).
The measured quantity column header is 'Hardness [HV]', subdivided into 'Hot-rolled' and '800 °C — Tempere' (last characters truncated by the image edge).
9Al-10Mn-1C hardness increases from 273 HV (hot-rolled) to 356 HV after 800 °C tempering.
12Al-10Mn-1C hardness is essentially unchanged by tempering: 401 HV hot-rolled versus 399 HV after 800 °C.
12Al-20Mn-1C hardness increases from 357 HV (hot-rolled) to 404 HV after 800 °C tempering, the largest absolute increase in the table.
12Al-30Mn1C hardness increases from 324 HV (hot-rolled) to 352 HV after 800 °C tempering.
The highest hot-rolled hardness in the table is 401 HV (12Al-10Mn-1C) and the highest tempered hardness is 404 HV (12Al-20Mn-1C).
The caption labels the table as an example of the hardening effects of cellular transformation and spinodal decomposition.
The citing text states that only the alloys tempered at 800 °C underwent cellular transformation and/or spinodal decomposition.
The citing text attributes the hardness increase to extensive κ + α + γ lamellar structures from cellular transformation plus spinodal decomposed γ, as exemplified by high Al and C with medium Mn.

The citing text states that increasing manganese to medium-high levels gives similar phases but less developed transformation, and that spinodal decomposition contributes to raising the alloy hardness level.
The citing text notes that even where inter-lamellar spacing is high (12Al-20Mn-1C, 12% Al) the hardening effects were consistent, matching the 357→404 HV increase in the table.
